clue.text: Supporter of fishermen in strike?

definitions.meaning: a fishing boat, which carries and so supports those who fish
to hit with the open hand

explanation.surface: A question about who backs fishermen during an industrial strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a traditional sailing fishing vessel, and also a sharp slap or blow.

clue.text: Perhaps left wood to make furniture

parts.note: left is one example of a side
a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: Someone may have left timber behind to build a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a dining-room cabinet for storing dishes.

clue.text: Further profit?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a gain

explanation.surface: Asking about yet more earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A GAIN for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means additionally or once more; as two words it is one more benefit.

clue.text: What chuck was to be innocent of (Macbeth)

definitions.text: What chuck was to be innocent of (Macbeth)

parts.words: What chuck was to be innocent of (Macbeth)
parts.note: Macbeth tells his wife, whom he calls dearest chuck, to be innocent of this about the planned murder of Banquo

explanation.surface: A quiz question on a line from Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'Be innocent of the knowledge, dearest chuck' (Macbeth III.ii); chuck is a term of endearment, not a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation fills in the missing noun meaning awareness or information.

clue.text: AA branch repairs many a vehicle

indicators.note: repairs suggests putting something back together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A local branch of the Automobile Association fixes many a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring breakdown service, so 'repairs' looks like its business rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Feature about pasture of S America

indicators.note: about means the facial feature goes round the pasture

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
a lea is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: A characteristic of South American grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilean means from Chile, a South American country.

clue.text: Isn't commonly concerned with direction of course

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
re means about or concerning
E is the compass direction east

explanation.surface: Someone colloquially denies interest in the course's direction.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE in Liverpool is the racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous horse-racing venue near Liverpool.

clue.text: Letter writer shows a bit of irritation

parts.note: taken as written
an itch is a small irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A correspondent's letter betrays some annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer shows' is only a link; 'Letter' is not a written message but a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Like the attempt to hold up Dr No by science

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: to hold means the attempt goes round the rest

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
No is short for number, taken here as written

explanation.surface: A Bond fan's plan to waylay Dr No through science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MONO into ONOM, which TRY holds: TRONOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the scientific study of the stars and planets.

clue.text: A feature of some sauce?

explanation.surface: An ingredient in certain sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheek is part of the face, and cheek is impudence, like sauce.

clue.text: Wag turns back on Scot — very severe

indicators.note: turns back says the joker's word is to be read from right to left

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag
taken as written
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A joker turns his back on a Scotsman in a severe way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns back' makes DRAC from CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian laws, after the Athenian lawgiver Draco, are excessively harsh.

clue.text: "The Count of Monte Cristo", perhaps

parts.note: both the name of a novel and a nobleman's rank are examples of what is wanted

explanation.surface: An example drawn from Dumas's famous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's name is a book title, and Count is itself a title of nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's name and a rank such as Count are both called this.

clue.text: Commonplace article written in work-room — returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole construction is read backwards
written in means the article is placed inside the room

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a room for work
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dull piece of writing produced in a workshop and sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' puts the article inside the room, and 'returned' turns the whole result round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banal is trite and ordinary, lacking originality.

clue.text: After a change of heart, carry on, operations for the Bank

indicators.note: a change of heart is read literally: the letters of heart are rearranged

parts.note: to work is to carry on or operate

explanation.surface: Someone having changed their mind resolves to keep going with banking business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a change of' rearranges the letters of the word heart. The 'Bank' is a mound of soil, not the Bank of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthwork is the excavating and piling of soil to build embankments.

clue.text: Desert players in a cricket side

indicators.note: in places the players inside the other two pieces

parts.note: taken as written
the on side is one half of a cricket field, the leg side
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Players walk out on a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to leave behind or forsake.

clue.text: A born composer — of water music?

parts.note: taken as written
Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music

explanation.surface: A newborn composer writing Handel-style water music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Handel's 'Water Music': a teetotaller's tune is water.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refuses alcohol and so drinks only water.

clue.text: Turn to account some brilliant achievement

definitions.meaning: to make use of or profit from

explanation.surface: Make use of a fine accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit is to put something to profitable use; an exploit is also a bold feat.

clue.text: A sort of naval overseer?

parts.note: read literally, a device on a submarine that sees over the waves

explanation.surface: A question about a ship's supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseer' suggests a supervisor, but it is a thing that sees over the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This optical tube lets a submerged crew see above the water.

clue.text: Toy found by tree — Dad went mad

indicators.note: went mad says the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A child's toy turns up by a tree and father is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went mad' rearranges BYTREEDAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed toy animal.

clue.text: Decline to get rid of the smell? -

definitions.meaning: a downward slope or a fall
read as ..., removing a scent or odour

explanation.surface: A question of refusing to remove an odour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as DE-SCENT: to take away a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a fall or decline; the second sense is a whimsical coinage.

clue.text: Upset at a number going to crib composition

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the whole run is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a cot is a child's crib

explanation.surface: Distressed at a figure heading for the cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns ATACCOT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece.

clue.text: Wandered through the East dry parts

indicators.note: parts, as a verb, means separates and rearranges the letters given

explanation.surface: A traveller roamed across the arid parts of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges EASTDRY; 'through the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strayed means roamed away from the proper path.

clue.text: Given comfort when fastened thus

parts.note: so means thus
laced means tied up, as a shoe

explanation.surface: A person was consoled after being tied up like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaced means consoled or comforted.

clue.text: The sort of joke that is feasible

definitions.meaning: a trick played on someone, rather than a verbal joke

explanation.surface: A joke that can actually be carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke is a prank; practical also means workable.

clue.text: Simple French food — about a pound

indicators.note: about means the bread goes round the pound

parts.note: pain is French for bread
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Uncomplicated French cooking costs about a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple or unadorned.

clue.text: Try to make sense of it

explanation.surface: Attempt to understand something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make sense of' is an idiom for understand, but here sense is a noun on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste is to sample, and taste is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Girl-friend follows point

indicators.note: follows places the friend after the compass point

parts.note: S is the compass point south
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend comes after the main point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl-friend' looks like one word but splits: Girl is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Fish without a pool

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the pool goes around the letter

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A fish out of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loach is a small freshwater fish.

clue.text: Embodiment of David's "triumph of hope over experience"?

definitions.text: Embodiment of David's "triumph of hope over experience"?

parts.words: Embodiment of David's "triumph of hope over experience"?
parts.note: Dr Johnson's phrase for a second marriage, applied to the second wife of Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A literary allusion to Dr Johnson's quip on remarrying.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson called a second marriage 'the triumph of hope over experience'; David Copperfield's second wife is Agnes Wickfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes Wickfield becomes David Copperfield's second wife in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Main stop in USA

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, so a stopping place for ships
a city in the United States, in Alaska

explanation.surface: A principal stopping point in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the old poetic word for the sea, not 'chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a place where ships moor; it is also Alaska's largest city.

clue.text: Servant is rude — man has to be replaced

indicators.note: has to be replaced asks for the letters to be put back in another order

explanation.surface: A rude employee must lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to be replaced' rearranges ISRUDEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a domestic employed to look after children.

clue.text: Polite sherry parties taking place in Surrey

indicators.note: parties, read as parts, says the letters come from within the words

explanation.surface: Genteel sherry gatherings held in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a well-off town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in the county of Surrey.
